item.title: Embracing the glitches in gravity could give us a unified theory of reality
item.description: Physicists have long struggled with their goal of making gravity a quantum force. A radical post-quantum approach might solve that problem – and clear up other cosmic mysteries, too

item.title: MIT Quantum Initiative launches postdoctoral fellowship program
item.description: The Institute welcomes its first cohort of QMIT Fellows this fall to advance interdisciplinary quantum research.

item.title: AI helps design new materials that work in the real world
item.description: The “CrysVCD” tool developed at MIT could cut the huge amounts of time and money spent on screening out chemically unstable designs.

item.title: MIT selected to lead new NSF materials research center
item.description: The Materials Research Science and Engineering Center unites researchers across disciplines to develop technologies for medical imaging, sustainable metals production, and next-generation electronics.

item.title: Astronomers catch a star slowly snacking on a brown dwarf, 300 light years away
item.description: The discovery reveals a new way that stars and planetary companions can interact.

item.title: Physicists watch a material’s electrons assemble, and reassemble, into coexisting phases
item.description: The study could help scientists understand how superconductivity and other more complex phenomena emerge in quantum materials.

item.title: Researchers make air-stable, ultrathin superconductors, for more scalable quantum devices
item.description: A new technique produces wafer-scale samples, overcoming a major roadblock to using these materials in quantum technologies.

item.title: MIT projects selected for funding under US Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission
item.description: Initial research projects advance national priorities across natural resources, manufacturing, nuclear physics, and more.

item.title: 对话诺奖评委潘嫱：从观察藻类到研究大脑，好奇心如何通向诺奖？
item.description: 2026年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖授予彼得·黑格曼（Peter Hegemann）、格奥尔格·纳格尔（Georg Nagel）和卡尔·戴瑟罗斯（Karl Deisseroth），表彰他们在光门控离子通道与光遗传学方面的发现。

item.title: 日本为何不断产生诺奖科学家？答案可能不在“培养”二字
item.description: 10月7日，2026年诺贝尔化学奖揭晓，76岁的日本化学家硤合宪三（Kenso Soai）与95岁的法国化学家亨利·卡甘（Henri Kagan）共同获奖，获奖原因是他们发现了不对称有机合成中的非线性效应和自催化现象。

item.title: The SPS turns 50
item.description: Protons, antiprotons, electrons, positrons, oxygen and lead ions… the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) has been juggling particles with ease for the past 50 years. By turns an accelerator, a collider and an injector, this versatile machine has seen generations of scientists pass through its doors, supplied dozens of experiments and given rise to groundbreaking technologies […]

item.title: Nobel prize in physics awarded for discovery of high-energy neutrinos
item.description: The 2026 Nobel prize in physics has been won by Francis Halzen for his work on neutrinos, which serve as 'ghost-like messengers from the cosmos'

item.description: Behind the scenes of CERN’s accelerators and detectors, millions of lines of code help turn particle collisions into scientific knowledge. item.title: Astronomers discover a brand-new type of astrophysical object: A black hole star
item.description: The mashup of a black hole and an enormous star has never been seen before and could explain the mysterious little red dots often found in deep-space images.

item.title: Jesse Thaler named director of the Laboratory for Nuclear Science
item.description: The professor of physics and inaugural director of the NSF AI Institute for Artificial Intelligence and Fundamental Interactions will lead LNS and continue his research in particle physics.

item.title: Boleslaw Wyslouch steps down as director of Laboratory for Nuclear Science
item.description: Wyslouch remains the director of the Bates Research and Engineering Center and will continue research on heavy ion collisions.

item.title: Scattering neutrinos to probe the fundamental laws of the universe
item.description: As she became integral to an international particle physics experiment, PhD student Faith Reyes found confidence in herself as a scientist.

item.title: Robotic lab sets up and runs optics experiments on demand
item.description: The autonomous system could speed up testing of high-tech materials for applications such as solar cells, sensors, video displays, and quantum technologies.

item.title: Podcast: SHASS’s special sauce
item.description: Established after World War II, the School of the Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences is an integral part of the MIT experience. Three faculty reflect on the school’s ongoing impact.

item.title: Study: Peptides can form well-defined structures in harsh, Venus-like conditions
item.description: New research offers support for the possibility that complex biological molecules could exist in the highly acidic environment of Venus’s cloud layer.

item.title: A new way to watch heat move through electronics
item.description: MIT researchers can now precisely measure how heat moves through multilayered materials like computer chips.

item.title: New artist residency program at MIT expands views of the cosmos
item.description: Inaugural artist Amy Karle will join astrophysicists at MIT’s Kavli Institute to explore questions about the universe and translate them into an immersive multimedia experience.

item.title: Looking beyond research
item.description: Professor Anna-Christina Eilers is “Committed to Caring” for building a culture around attentiveness and community.

item.title: MIT student leaders: Q&A with men’s soccer captain Dilin Meloni
item.description: The rising senior is passionate about soccer, nuclear fusion, and advocating on behalf of his fellow student-athletes at MIT.

item.title: Diffuse puffs of “missing” matter surround most galaxies
item.description: An MIT-led team used bright radio bursts to illuminate a vast source of matter that was previously unaccounted for.

item.title: How an influx of salt may affect microbial ecosystems
item.description: As sea levels rise and saltwater seeps into freshwater, stressed aquatic populations may retain overall growth even as diversity declines, MIT scientists find.

item.title: Many black holes had past lives, new research shows
item.description: Physicists have found signs of colliding black holes that are themselves products of previous black hole smash-ups.
